subsystems.name: Sensing elements
subsystems.role: convert a physical quantity — temperature, humidity, pressure, a trace gas, particulates, ground motion — into a signal.

subsystems.name: Node electronics and power
subsystems.role: let each unit run unattended for years without maintenance.
parts: solar, vibration or thermal energy harvester

subsystems.name: Communication mesh
subsystems.role: relay readings hop by hop from node to gateway without a per-node subscription.

subsystems.name: Deployment platforms
subsystems.role: put nodes into the atmosphere, ocean, soil and crust.

subsystems.name: Aggregation infrastructure
subsystems.role: collect, timestamp and archive the data stream.

subsystems.name: Assimilation and modelling
subsystems.role: turn billions of noisy readings into a usable picture of the planet.

buildSteps.title: Fix the measurement targets
buildSteps.detail: Decide which variables matter, at what accuracy, and over what volume — for example air temperature to a fraction of a degree, or ground motion to micrometres, per cubic metre of the region of interest.

buildSteps.title: Design a node on a chip
buildSteps.detail: Combine a MEMS sensing element, a low-power microcontroller, radio and antenna into a package a few millimetres across, using the same batch semiconductor and thin-film processes that made sensors cheap in phones.

buildSteps.title: Solve the power budget
buildSteps.detail: A node that cannot be reached must harvest its own energy — a few square millimetres of solar cell, a vibration or thermal harvester — and sleep almost all the time, waking only to sense and transmit.

buildSteps.title: Build the mesh software
buildSteps.detail: Write routing that lets nodes discover neighbours, forward each other's packets and survive failures, with synchronised clocks so readings can be compared across the grid.

buildSteps.title: Manufacture at throwaway cost
buildSteps.detail: Scale production so a unit costs a small fraction of the data it produces; flexible printed electronics and roll-to-roll processes would be needed for volume far beyond current sensor markets.

buildSteps.title: Disperse the first region
buildSteps.detail: Release nodes from balloons and drones over a chosen area and drop fixed stations, seismic sensors and ocean drifters, then let the mesh self-organise around gateways.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate against references
buildSteps.detail: Cross-check every cheap sensor against reference instruments such as radiosondes, seismometers and satellite measurements, and model drift so long-term trends remain trustworthy.

buildSteps.title: Assimilate into models
buildSteps.detail: Feed the stream into numerical weather, climate and geophysical models that blend observations with physics, the same way today's sparse networks are used but at far finer resolution.

buildSteps.title: Operate, replenish, retire
buildSteps.detail: Continuously replace failed nodes and harvest or recover expended ones, because littering the atmosphere and ocean with persistent devices would create a pollution problem of its own.

prerequisites.why: the smartphone industry already mass-produces accurate accelerometers, pressure and gas sensors.
demonstrated in small devices, but years of unattended life in cold, wet or dark conditions is not solved.
standards such as LoRa exist for thousands of nodes per gateway; trillions of nodes and global relay remain untested.
small satellites can collect data from remote ground terminals, but capacity and cost for a planet-wide grid are unproven.
blending billions of observations into real-time models demands computing and algorithms beyond today's operational systems.
dispersing huge numbers of devices into air, soil and sea requires materials that degrade or can be retrieved.

pathway.milestone: sparse reference networks: weather balloons, the Argo fleet of ocean-profiling floats, the Global Seismographic Network, and satellite gravity and radar missions
pathway.unlocks: global climate and hazard monitoring at coarse resolution.

pathway.milestone: dense regional meshes of cheap sensors in cities, catchments and fault zones, with commercial satellite links for the remotest sites
pathway.unlocks: street-scale air quality, flood and landslide early warning.

pathway.milestone: targeted aerial and marine dispersion of miniature disposable sensors over a test region
pathway.unlocks: direct measurement of the atmosphere's fine structure, where most uncertainty in weather and climate lies.

pathway.milestone: a continuously refreshed globe-spanning grid feeding digital-twin models in real time
pathway.unlocks: much sharper prediction of storms, quakes and long-term change — and the evidence base for any deliberate intervention, though sensing alone cannot control climate.
